fr.elements: Main Building; Vehicle Parking Area; Vehicle Parking Area; Front Driveway; Internal Drive Aisle; Landscaped Area; Front Entry Area; Pedestrian Walkways; Street Frontage; Roof System
fr.considerations: Multiple Access Points; Limited Rear Access; Dense Vegetation; Vehicle Congestion
fr.recommendations: Coordinating with property management to establish and maintain clear secondary access routes could improve responder movement, particularly given the limited access conditions observed at the rear of the property. Addressing vehicle congestion within parking areas and drive aisles would support apparatus maneuvering and may enhance staging capabilities during emergency operations. Managing dense vegetation along pedestrian walkways, entry areas, and the perimeter could improve responder visibility and ground-level navigation throughout the site. Clearly marking or designating access points along the street frontage may assist arriving units in identifying optimal entry routes and coordinating an effective operational approach.

wildfire.conditions: Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Scattered Shrubs; Vegetation Adjacent to Structure; Vegetation Adjacent to Access Route; Mixed Vegetation Cover; Irrigated Landscape; Defensible Space; Open Fuel Break; Brush Adjacent to Structure
wildfire.recommendations: Reducing the continuity of vegetation between tree clusters, scattered trees, and shrubs could improve fuel separation and limit the opportunity for fire to move toward structures. Managing brush and other vegetation growing immediately adjacent to structures would help reduce direct fuel exposure at the structure perimeter and could improve defensible space conditions. Similarly, addressing vegetation growing along the access route may support firefighter access and improve conditions for suppression operations. The existing irrigated landscape, open fuel break, and established defensible space areas represent meaningful assets that should be preserved and expanded where possible, as these features contribute to fuel continuity reduction and overall wildfire resilience. Continuing to manage mixed vegetation cover across the property, particularly where dense patches connect to structural improvements, would further support long-term preparedness and help maintain the value of existing fuel breaks and open areas already present on the property.
